issues.description: Expected class: The problem statement and the solution repository define a public class named 'Farm' (the UML and solution use 'Farm' with a List<Animal> and methods addAnimal, feedAllAnimals, singFarmSong). Template contradiction: src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java in the template declares a class named 'AnimalFarm' (line 3) and also contains a duplicated package declaration and a nested/duplicated class fragment (package declaration at line 10 and a second 'public class AnimalFarm' at line 12). This mismatch (class name and malformed file contents) prevents students from implementing or compiling the intended 'Farm' class and makes it unclear how to map the UML/tasks to the starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the malformed template file with a proper stub matching the exercise specification: declare package de.tum.cit.ase; declare public class Farm (not AnimalFarm). Remove the duplicated package declaration and duplicated/nested class fragments. Provide the expected members as stubs: private List<Animal> animals; a public no-argument constructor that initializes animals = new ArrayList<>(); public List<Animal> getAnimals(); public void setAnimals(List<Animal>); public void addAnimal(Animal a); public void feedAllAnimals(); public void singFarmSong(); and a private helper singFarmSongVerse(Animal). Keep method bodies as simple stubs (or TODOs) so students can implement them, but ensure the file compiles and the class name matches the problem statement and solution.
